threads.text: The first human heart transplant happened in which country — United States, South Africa or United Kingdom? Almost everyone picks America. The surgeon became famous overnight, and his patient's new heart beat with no nerve link to the brain at all.

intent: Medical-history reveal told like a newsreel: place, date, the man, the number of days, then the body fact nobody knows.

v04.text: South Africa. Cape Town, December 1967: surgeon Christiaan Barnard gave Louis Washkansky a new heart.

v05.text: The patient lived 18 days. The heart worked; it was pneumonia that killed him.

v06.text: Stanford had done the research, but Barnard got there first, and was famous overnight.

v07.text: A transplanted heart has no nerves linking it to the brain. It beats on its own pacemaker, inside the muscle.

v08.text: Not where you thought. Follow us.

research.topic: The first human heart transplant: Groote Schuur Hospital, Cape Town, South Africa, 3 December 1967 (Christiaan Barnard; patient Louis Washkansky lived 18 days)

myths.myth: The first heart transplant was performed in the United States.
myths.reality: US teams (Shumway, Lower) developed the technique, but the first human-to-human transplant was Barnard's in Cape Town on 3 December 1967; the first US adult transplant followed in January 1968 (Shumway, Stanford).

wiki_barnard.title: Christiaan Barnard
wiki_barnard.notes: performed the world's first human-to-human heart transplant 3 December 1967 at Groote Schuur, Cape Town; became an international celebrity

stanford_med.title: Norman Shumway and the history of heart transplantation
stanford_med.notes: Shumway's lab developed the technique over a decade; first US adult heart transplant 6 January 1968 at Stanford, a month after Barnard

wiki_shumway.title: Norman Shumway
wiki_shumway.notes: Stanford surgeon, pioneer of heart transplantation research; first US adult heart transplant January 1968

statpearls_denerv.title: Physiology, Cardiac Denervation / Heart transplant physiology
statpearls_denerv.notes: the transplanted heart is denervated — no autonomic nerve connection to the recipient's nervous system; rhythm is set by the donor sinoatrial node (intrinsic pacemaker)

cleveland_transplant.title: Heart Transplant
cleveland_transplant.notes: a transplanted heart has no nerve connections; it beats via its own SA node and responds to hormones rather than nerve signals

pmc_barnard50.title: The first human heart transplant and further advances in cardiac transplantation at Groote Schuur Hospital
pmc_barnard50.notes: Brink & Hassoulas 2017: Washkansky operated 3 Dec 1967; good cardiac function; died day 18 of pneumonia (Pseudomonas) under heavy immunosuppression
